questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the opposite of cháng?
What age range does niánqīng rén usually mean?
Which word is zǒng often followed by?
What is the SECOND use of zǒng, as seen in exchange 4?
Write the Chinese for "Children will be children."
Write the Chinese for "It's better to come a little late than not to come at all."

answers.answer_text: Lái wǎn yìdiǎnr zǒng bǐ bù lái hǎo.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "How long is the Great Wall?"
Give three English translations for the second meaning of zǒng.

answers.answer_text: Any three of: "after all," "surely," "in any case," "when all is said and done," "inevitably," "eventually."

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Someday he will surely come back."

answers.answer_text: Zǒng yǒu yìtiān, tā huì huíláide.

articles.text:
4. A: Zuótian Xiǎo Míng gěi ta       Yesterday Xiǎo Míng wrote a letter
      nǚpéngyou xiě xìn, xiěde        to his girl friend, and it was
      hǎo cháng!                      really long!
   B: Niánqīng rén zǒng shi          Young people are always young
      niánqīng rén. Wǒ niánqīngde     people; when I was young I was
      shíhou yě shi zhèiyàng, nǐ      like that too, have you forgotten?
      wàng le?

Notes on No. 4

cháng: "to be long" in physical length, or in some cases, time. The opposite of cháng is duǎn, "to be short."

Chángchéng yǒu duō cháng?        How long is the Great Wall?
Yǒu liùqiānduō gōnglǐ (cháng).   It's over six thousand kilometers.
Wǒ hěn cháng shíjiān méi         I haven't seen him in a long time.
kànjian ta le.

niánqīng: "to be young." Niánqīng rén usually means people from the teens through the twenties.

Tā niánqīngde shíhou bǐ xiànzài  When she was young she was even more
gèng hǎo kàn.                    beautiful than now.

zǒng: "always, invariably." Like other adverbs such as zhēn and hái, zǒng is often followed by shi.

Nǐ zǒngshi wèn wo wèntí.         You always ask me questions.
Zhèizhǒng shìqing zǒngshi ràng   This type of thing always makes one
rén hěn gāoxìng.                 very happy.

Zǒng bù, "always not...," is one way of saying "never":

Tā zǒng bù xǐhuan biérén wèn ta  He never likes other people to ask
jiālide shì.                     about his family.

Zǒng has ANOTHER USE, which is the one you see in exchange 4: instead of meaning literally "on every occasion," zǒng is used to suggest that a certain state of affairs should be OBVIOUSLY TRUE, regardless of other circumstances. Translations depend on the context: "after all, surely, always, in any case, when all is said and done, inevitably, eventually."

Xiǎoháizi zǒng shi xiǎoháizi,    Children will be children; after they
dàle jiu hǎo le.                 grow up it will be better.
Nǐ bú jiè wo, wǒ zài zhèr        If you won't lend it to me, at least
kànkan zǒng kěyi ba?             I can read it here, can't I?
Nǐ shi Měiguo rén, nǐ zǒng bù    You're an American, you can't very
néng bù zhīdào Dézhōu zài        well not know where Texas is,
nǎr ba?!                         can you?!
Zǒng yǒu yìtiān, tā huì          Someday he will surely come back.
huíláide.
Lái wǎn yìdiǎnr zǒng bǐ bù lái   It's better to come a little late
hǎo.                             than not to come at all.
